title: CL-CLIP: CLIP-Based Continual Learning Framework with Cost-Volume Category Decoupling for Object Detection

problem.summary: Continual Object Detection (COD) requires a detector to acquire new categories over time while preserving previously learned ones.
statements: Continual Object Detection (COD) requires a detector to acquire new categories over time while preserving previously learned ones.
This goal is closely related to open-vocabulary detection, since both settings require reasoning over categories that are not fully covered by the annotations available at the current training stage.

Recent CLIP-based open-vocabulary detectors have shown strong zero-shot generalization, and frameworks such as F-ViT demonstrate that vision-language pretraining can provide powerful zero-shot detection ability for unseen categories.

solution.summary: Continual Object Detection (COD) aims to learn novel categories from a task stream while preserving previously acquired detection ability [15, 25, 23, 8].
solution.approach: Continual Object Detection (COD) aims to learn novel categories from a task stream while preserving previously acquired detection ability [15, 25, 23, 8].
components: Unlike image classification, however, COD must handle multi-object scenes in which old and new categories co-occur spatially.

When the model is updated on a new task, previously learned objects appear without annotations and are treated as background, rapidly eroding old-class decision boundaries and causing severe catastrophic forgetting.
Existing COD methods address this problem through knowledge distillation [23, 8, 10, 29], regularization [12, 31, 21], replay [9, 20, 1], and pseudo-labeling [35].
